A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel semi-supervised parsing model that can be trained efficiently and that outperforms the state-of-the-art on three different languages.
our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on English and French, and competitive performance on Swedish, while being trained on only 5% labeled training data.
our method is able to improve the performance of a parser trained with a small amount of labeled data by leveraging unlabeled texts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to learn a generative model that captures the syntactic structure of natural language, and use it to improve parsing accuracy.

, in the semi-supervised setting, it is beneficial to model the distribution over syntactic trees as a mixture of a large number of latent variables, which are sampled during training, and which can be interpreted as latent syntactic structures.
